title: Quantifying and Estimating the Predictability Upper Bound of Univariate Numeric Time Series

problem.claim: The work addresses how to quantify the intrinsic predictability of a univariate numeric time series and determine how close prediction algorithms are to theoretically achievable performance.

gap.claim: Intrinsic predictability had previously been computed only for symbolic time series, despite most real-world time series being numeric.

contributions.claim: The authors propose a method for quantifying and estimating the predictability upper bound of univariate numeric time series.
The technique uses the relationship between entropy and predictability, specifically the entropy rate of a time series, to compute the predictability upper bound.
The authors develop entropy-rate estimators for numeric data using tolerance thresholds for matching numeric values.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their method for quantifying and estimating the predictability upper bound of univariate numeric time series as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the predictability upper bound is an effective upper bound characterizing the intrinsic predictability of a time series.

The authors report formal proofs and experimental validation comparing the predictability upper bound with the prediction accuracy of different state-of-the-art models on real-world datasets from different domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Intrinsic predictability describes how well an ideal algorithm could potentially predict a time series from its data.
Computing intrinsic predictability can indicate remaining optimization potential for prediction algorithms.
The authors identify the lack of methods for numeric time series, propose a predictability upper bound, and develop entropy-based estimators using numeric matching tolerances.
The authors report theoretical and experimental evaluation against state-of-the-art prediction models on real-world datasets from multiple domains.

source_observation.claim: A predictability upper bound can be used to characterize intrinsic predictability and indicate whether further model optimization may be possible.

interpretation.claim: Estimating an attainable-performance boundary can help distinguish limitations imposed by the data from limitations of the prediction algorithm.

application.claim: Use an entropy-based predictability estimate as a diagnostic when assessing forecasting performance for univariate numeric time series.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves outside univariate numeric time series or under conditions not represented by the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the mathematical definition or formula for the predictability upper bound.
The abstract does not specify the tolerance-threshold procedure or estimator configurations.
The abstract does not report quantitative experimental results, dataset names, or model names.
The abstract does not provide details of the formal proofs or their assumptions.
